sentences.zh: 趙宗儒趙宗儒，字秉文。

translations.literal: Zhao Zongru—Zhao Zongru, courtesy name Bingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zongru, whose courtesy name was Bingwen.

sentences.zh: 八代祖彤，仕後魏為征南將軍。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Tong served the Later Wei as General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor eight generations back, named Tong, had served the Later Wei as General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 父驊，為秘書少監。

translations.literal: His father Hua was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hua held the post of Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宗儒舉進士，初授弘文館校書郎。

translations.literal: Zongru passed the jinshi examination and was first appointed collator at the Hongwen Library.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru passed the jinshi examination and was first appointed as a collator in the Hongwen Library.

sentences.zh: 滿歲，又以書判入高等，補陸渾主簿。

translations.literal: When his term was complete, he again entered the upper grade by document examination and was appointed chief clerk of Luhun.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he again scored in the top tier on the document examination and was appointed chief clerk of Luhun County.

sentences.zh: 數月，征拜右拾遺，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned and appointed Right Reminder, serving as a Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was called to court and appointed Right Reminder, and also served as a Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 時父驊秘書少監，與父並命，出於一日，當時榮之。

translations.literal: At the time his father Hua was Vice Director of the Secretariat; father and son were both appointed on the same day, which was then considered an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his father Hua was Vice Director of the Secretariat, and father and son received appointments on the same day—a distinction much remarked upon at the time.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，轉屯田員外郎，內職如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms, while his inner-court duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In 783 he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of State Farms while retaining his inner-court posts.

sentences.zh: 居父憂，免喪，授司門、司勛二員外郎。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his father; when mourning ended he was appointed Vice Director of both the Bureau of Gatekeepers and the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his father, upon the end of mourning he was appointed vice director in both the Bureau of Gatekeepers and the Bureau of Merits.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年，領考功事，定百吏考績，黜陟公當，無所畏避。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenyuan he took charge of examination affairs, fixed the performance ratings of all officials, and demotions and promotions were fair, without fear or favor.
translations.idiomatic: In 790 he took charge of the Bureau of Examination, set the performance ratings of the entire bureaucracy, and made promotions and demotions with impartial fairness, unafraid of anyone.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中獨孤良器、殿中侍御史杜倫，各以過黜之。

translations.literal: Dugu Liangqi, Director of the Right Department, and Du Lun, Palace Investigating Censor, were each demoted for their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Liangqi of the Right Department and Du Lun, a palace censor, were each demoted for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞裴郁、禦名中丞盧紹，比皆考中上，宗儒貶之中中。

translations.literal: Pei Yu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Lu Shao, Vice Censor-in-Chief—in both cases their ratings had been upper middle; Zongru reduced them to middle middle.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Lu Shao, Vice Censor-in-Chief, had both been rated upper-middle; Zongru downgraded each to middle-middle.

sentences.zh: 又秘書少監鄭雲逵考其同官孫昌裔入上下，宗儒復入中上。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zheng Yunkui, Vice Director of the Secretariat, had rated his colleague Sun Changyi as upper-lower; Zongru changed it back to middle-upper.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director of the Secretariat Zheng Yunkui had rated his fellow official Sun Changyi upper-lower, Zongru revised the rating to middle-upper.

sentences.zh: 凡考之中上者，不過五十人，余多減入中中。

translations.literal: Of all those rated middle-upper, no more than fifty were allowed; the rest were mostly reduced to middle-middle.
translations.idiomatic: He allowed no more than fifty officials to receive a middle-upper rating; most others were downgraded to middle-middle.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞而善之，遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: Dezong heard of this and approved; he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Examination.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong heard of this he approved, and Zongru was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Examination.

sentences.zh: 丁夏憂，終喪，授吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 795 he was transferred to Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與諫議大夫崔損同日以本官同中書門下平章事，俱賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on the same day as Remonstrance Counselor Cui Sun, he assumed the same post as jointly Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and both were granted purple-gold fish tally pouches.
translations.idiomatic: In 796 he and Remonstrance Counselor Cui Sun were on the same day appointed joint Grand Councilors under the Secretariat-Chancellery in their existing ranks, and both were granted purple-gold fish tally pouches.

sentences.zh: 十四年，罷相，為右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was removed as councilor and made Right Senior Companion of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 798 he left the chancellorship and was appointed Right Senior Companion of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 宗儒端居守道，勤奉朝請而已，德宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Zongru lived uprightly and held to the Way, attending court diligently and nothing more; Dezong heard of this and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru lived quietly, clung to the proper path, and attended court with steady diligence and little else; Dezong heard of this and praised him.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遷吏部侍郎，召見，勞之曰：「知卿閉關六年，故有此拜。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel; summoned for audience, [the emperor] comforted him, saying: "Knowing that you have kept to seclusion for six years, this appointment is therefore made.
translations.idiomatic: In 804 he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel. When summoned before the throne, the emperor said to him with kindness, "Knowing that you have kept to your seclusion for six years, you have earned this appointment.

sentences.zh: 曩者與先臣並命，尚念之耶？」

translations.literal: In those days [your appointment] together with your late father—do you still remember?
translations.idiomatic: Do you still remember when you and your late father were appointed on the same day?

sentences.zh: 宗儒因俯伏流涕。

translations.literal: Zongru thereupon prostrated himself in tears.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru bowed low to the ground and wept.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，順宗命為德宗哀冊文，辭頗淒惋。

translations.literal: When Dezong died, Shunzong ordered him to compose Dezong's lamentation text; the wording was quite mournful and poignant.
translations.idiomatic: After Dezong's death, Shunzong charged him with drafting the lamentation for the late emperor's burial register; the language was deeply sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 元和初，檢校禮部尚書，判東都尚書省事、兼御史大夫，充東都留守、畿汝都防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was made Acting Minister of Rites, directing the Eastern Capital Department of State Affairs office, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, serving as Eastern Capital Regent and Metropolitan Ji-Ru Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe reign he was appointed Acting Minister of Rites, with charge of the Eastern Capital Secretariat office, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Eastern Capital Regent, and Metropolitan Defense Commissioner for the Ji and Ru circuits.

sentences.zh: 入為禮部、戶部二尚書，尋檢校吏部尚書，守江陵尹、兼御史大夫、荊南節度營田觀察等使。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Minister of both Rites and Revenue; soon he was made Acting Minister of Personnel, holding Jiangling as magistrate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Jingnan Military Commissioner, Agricultural Commissioner, and Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of Rites and of Revenue, then soon appointed Acting Minister of Personnel as magistrate of Jiangling, with concurrent posts as Censor-in-Chief and Jingnan military, agricultural, and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 散冗食之戍二千人。

translations.literal: He dismissed two thousand garrison troops maintained as superfluous.
translations.idiomatic: He discharged two thousand superfluous garrison troops from the payroll.

sentences.zh: 六年，又入為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again entered [the capital] as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was again recalled as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 八年，轉檢校吏部尚書、興元尹、兼御史大夫，充山南西道節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Personnel, Xingyuan Magistrate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, serving as Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Acting Minister of Personnel and magistrate of Xingyuan, with concurrent posts as Censor-in-Chief and Shannan West military and observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年，召拜御史大夫，俄遷檢校右僕射、河中尹、兼御史大夫、晉絳慈隰節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief; soon he was transferred to Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Hezhong Magistrate, concurrently Censor-in-Chief and Jin-jiang-ci-li Military and Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief; soon after he was made Acting Right Vice Director, magistrate of Hezhong, and concurrent military and observation commissioner for Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Li.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮後，擅用供軍錢八千余貫，坐罰一月俸。

translations.literal: After he went to his command, he appropriated more than eight thousand strings of army-supply funds without authorization and was penalized one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: After taking up his post he had diverted more than eight thousand strings of army-supply funds without authorization and was fined one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 十一年七月，入為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year he entered [the capital] as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year he was recalled as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 九月，改太子少傅，權知吏部尚書銓事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with temporary charge of the Bureau of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given temporary charge of personnel selection as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以初釋服，令尚書省官試先朝所征集應制舉人。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, because he had just ended mourning, he ordered officials of the Department of State Affairs to examine the special-decree examination candidates gathered by the previous court.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong acceded, having just ended his mourning period, he ordered Department of State Affairs officials to examine the special-decree candidates whom the previous reign had summoned.

sentences.zh: 宗儒奏曰：「準今月十五日敕：比者先朝征集應制人等，已及時限，恐皆來自遠方，難於久住，酌宜審事，遂委有司定日就試。

translations.literal: Zongru memorialized: "According to the edict of the fifteenth of this month: the special-decree candidates gathered by the previous court have reached the time limit; fearing that all have come from distant places and find it hard to stay long, it was deemed appropriate to review the matter carefully, and the responsible offices were entrusted to set a date for the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru submitted a memorial: "Pursuant to the edict of the fifteenth of this month: the special-decree candidates whom the late court had summoned have reached the deadline. Fearing that most have come from afar and cannot remain long, the throne judged it prudent to review the matter and charged the responsible offices with setting a date for the examination.

sentences.zh: 如聞所集之人多已分散，須知審的，然後裁定，宜令所司商量聞奏者。

translations.literal: As I hear, most of those gathered have already dispersed; the facts must be verified clearly, and only then may a decision be made. The responsible offices should be ordered to deliberate and report.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that most of those summoned have already dispersed; the facts must be verified before any decision, and the responsible offices should deliberate and report back.

sentences.zh: 伏以制科所設，本在親臨，南省試人，亦非舊典。

translations.literal: I submit that the special-decree examinations were instituted for the emperor's personal presence; having the Southern Directorate examine candidates is also not an old precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The special-decree examinations were established for the emperor's personal oversight; entrusting the examination to the Southern Directorate is likewise not established precedent.

sentences.zh: 今覃恩既畢，庶政惟新。

translations.literal: Now that the general amnesty is complete, all ordinary government is renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the general amnesty has been proclaimed, every branch of government is being renewed.

sentences.zh: 況山陵日近，公務繁迫，待問之士，就試非多。

translations.literal: Moreover, the imperial tomb rites draw near, official business is pressing, and of the candidates awaiting examination, not many would actually take the test.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, with the imperial tomb rites approaching and official business pressing, few of the candidates awaiting examination would in fact present themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，恐須權罷。」

translations.literal: Your subjects have deliberated and fear the examination should be suspended for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants have deliberated and believe the examination should be suspended for the present.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 復拜太子少傅，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with charge of the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年二月，檢校右僕射，守太常卿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changqing he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, holding the post of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 821 he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director while retaining the directorship of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太常有《師子樂》，備五方之色，非會朝聘享不作，幼君荒誕，伶官縱肆，中人掌教坊者移牒取之。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices possessed the "Lion Music," furnished with the colors of the five directions; it was not performed except at court assemblies, audiences, or tribute receptions. The young ruler was dissolute; actors ran riot, and a eunuch in charge of the Music Academy sent a transfer document to take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices possessed the Lion Music, arrayed in the colors of the five directions, which was performed only at court assemblies, audiences, or tribute ceremonies. The young emperor was dissolute; actors ran wild, and a eunuch superintendent of the Music Academy sent an official request to take possession of it.

sentences.zh: 宗儒不敢違，以狀白宰相。

translations.literal: Zongru did not dare refuse and reported the matter in a memorial to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru did not dare refuse and reported the matter to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 宰相以為事在有司執守，不合關白。

translations.literal: The chief ministers held that the matter lay with the responsible office to uphold and was not something to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers held that the responsible office should enforce the rules on its own and that there was no need to report upward.

sentences.zh: 以宗儒怯不任事，改太子少師。

translations.literal: Because Zongru was timid and unfit for office, he was changed to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Zongru timid and unfit for responsibility, the court transferred him to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，遷太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he was transferred to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 825 he was promoted to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 昭肅晏駕，為大明宮留守。

translations.literal: When Zhaosu [Jingzong] died, he served as regent of the Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong died, he was appointed regent of the Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，拜檢校司空、兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 830 he was appointed Acting Minister of Works and Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 文宗召見，諮以理道。

translations.literal: Wenzong summoned him for audience and consulted him on the principles of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong summoned him and asked his counsel on the principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「堯、舜之化，慈儉而已。

translations.literal: He replied: "The transformation of Yao and Shun lay in compassion and frugality alone.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The rule of Yao and Shun rested on compassion and frugality alone.

sentences.zh: 願陛下守而勿失。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty hold to them and not let them slip away.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty hold to them and never let them slip away.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Wenzong commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong praised his answer and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 五年，宋申錫被誣，上召師保已下議其刑。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Song Shenxi was slandered; the emperor summoned the tutors and guardians and those below to deliberate on his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Song Shenxi was falsely accused; the emperor summoned the heir apparent's tutors and guardians and the ranks below to deliberate on his punishment.

sentences.zh: 上以宗儒高年，宣令不拜。

translations.literal: Because Zongru was advanced in years, the emperor proclaimed that he need not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zongru was of advanced age, the emperor directed that he need not perform the bow.

sentences.zh: 尋拜疏請老。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔以司空致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict granted him retirement with the rank of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict granted him retirement with the honorary rank of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月卒，年八十七，廢朝，冊贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year he died at age eighty-seven; court audiences were suspended, and by patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died that ninth month at the age of eighty-seven; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 宗儒以文學進，前後三鎮方任，八領選部，略於儀矩，切於治生，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: Zongru advanced through literary learning; he thrice held regional commands and eight times headed the selection bureau. He was somewhat lax in ritual propriety and keen on managing livelihood; contemporary opinion therefore thought somewhat less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru had risen through literary accomplishment, held three regional commands in succession, and headed the selection bureau eight times. He was somewhat careless of ritual propriety and keen on managing his livelihood, for which contemporaries thought somewhat less of him.

sentences.zh: 竇易直竇易直，字宗玄，京兆人。

translations.literal: Dou Yizhi—Dou Yizhi, courtesy name Zongxuan, a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi, whose courtesy name was Zongxuan, was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖元昌，彭州九瀧縣令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanchang was magistrate of Jiulong County in Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanchang had been magistrate of Jiulong County in Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父彧，廬州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yu was prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 易直舉明經，為秘書省校書郎，再以判入等，授藍田尉。

translations.literal: Yizhi passed the mingjing examination and was made collator in the Secretariat; again entering the upper grade by document examination, he was appointed defender of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi passed the mingjing examination and was appointed collator in the Secretariat; after again scoring in the top tier on the document examination, he was appointed defender of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 累歷右司、兵部、吏部三郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as director in the Right Department and in the Bureaus of War and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as director in the Right Department and in the Bureaus of War and of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 811 he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 謝日，賜緋魚袋。

translations.literal: On the day of his thanksgiving audience he was granted a scarlet fish tally pouch.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he thanked the throne for his appointment he was granted a scarlet fish tally pouch.

sentences.zh: 八年，改給事中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was changed to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 九月，出為陜虢都防禦觀察使，仍賜紫。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he went out as Metropolitan Shan-Guo Defense and Observation Commissioner, and was again granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was sent out as Metropolitan Defense and Observation Commissioner for Shan and Guo, and was again granted the purple robe.

sentences.zh: 入為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 萬年尉韓晤奸贓事發，易直令曹官韋正晤訊之，得贓三十萬。

translations.literal: When the bribery of Han Wu, defender of Wannian, came to light, Yizhi ordered the bureau official Wei Zhengwu to investigate and uncovered three hundred thousand in illicit gains.
translations.idiomatic: When the bribery of Han Wu, defender of Wannian, came to light, Yizhi ordered the bureau official Wei Zhengwu to investigate and uncovered three hundred thousand in illicit gains.

sentences.zh: 上意其未盡，詔重鞫，坐贓三百萬，貶易直金州刺史，正晤長流昭州。

translations.literal: The emperor thought the case incomplete and ordered a re-examination; the amount of bribery was fixed at three million, Yizhi was demoted to prefect of Jin Prefecture, and Zhengwu was exiled far to Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected the investigation incomplete and ordered a new inquiry; the bribery was fixed at three million, Yizhi was demoted to prefect of Jin Prefecture, and Zhengwu was exiled to distant Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十三年六月，遷宣州刺史、宣歙池都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to prefect of Xuan Prefecture and Metropolitan Xuan-She-Chi Training, Observation, and other Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the thirteenth year he was made prefect of Xuan and Metropolitan Training and Observation Commissioner for Xuan, She, and Chi.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年七月，汴州將李絺逐其帥李願，易直聞之，欲出官物以賞軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Changqing the Bianzhou general Li Qi expelled his commander Li Yuan; when Yizhi heard of it he wished to disburse official goods to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 822 the Bianzhou general Li Qi expelled his commander Li Yuan; when Yizhi heard of it he wished to disburse official goods to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 或謂易直曰：「賞給無名，卻恐生患。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Yizhi: "Rewards given without cause may instead breed trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Yizhi, "Rewards given without proper cause may instead breed trouble.

sentences.zh: 乃已。

translations.literal: He thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 軍士已聞之。

translations.literal: The soldiers had already heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers had already heard of it.

sentences.zh: 時江、淮旱，水淺，轉運司錢帛委積不能漕，州將王國清指以為賞，激諷州兵謀亂。

translations.literal: At the time the Yangzi and Huai regions suffered drought; the water was shallow, and money and silks accumulated by the transport office could not be shipped by canal. The prefectural general Wang Guoqing pointed to them as rewards and incited the prefectural troops to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi and Huai regions were then in drought; the waterways were shallow, and money and silks accumulated by the transport office could not be moved by canal. The prefectural general Wang Guoqing pointed to these stores as promised rewards and incited the prefectural troops to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 先事有告者，乃收國清下獄。

translations.literal: Someone reported the matter beforehand, and Guoqing was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported the plot beforehand, Guoqing was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 其黨數千，大呼入獄中，篡取國清而出之，因欲大剽。

translations.literal: His partisans, several thousand strong, shouted and stormed the prison, seized Guoqing and freed him, and then wished to loot on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand of his partisans stormed the prison shouting, seized Guoqing and freed him, and then prepared for large-scale pillage.

sentences.zh: 易直登樓謂將吏曰：「能誅為亂者，每獲一人，賞十萬。」

translations.literal: Yizhi mounted the tower and said to the generals and officials: "Whoever can kill those making rebellion—ten thousand for each man taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi mounted the tower and told the generals and officials, "Whoever kills a rebel will receive ten thousand for each man taken.

sentences.zh: 眾喜，倒戈擊亂黨，並擒之。

translations.literal: The crowd rejoiced, turned their weapons on the rebel faction, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: The troops rejoiced, turned their weapons on the rebels, and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 國清等三百余人，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Guoqing and more than three hundred others were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqing and more than three hundred others were all beheaded.

sentences.zh: 九月，以李德裕代還，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Li Deyu replaced him and he returned [to the capital] as Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Deyu replaced him; he returned to the capital as Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一月，改戶部，兼御史大夫，判度支。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was changed to the Ministry of Revenue, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, with charge of the Directorate of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, with concurrent posts as Censor-in-Chief and director of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，以本官同平章事，判使如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was made jointly Grand Councilor in his existing post, with his commissioner's duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed joint Grand Councilor in his existing rank, retaining his treasury duties.

sentences.zh: 改門下侍郎，封晉陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Chancellery and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年七月，罷判度支。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Baoli he was removed from charge of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 825 he was relieved of his treasury duties.

sentences.zh: 大和二年十月罷相，檢校左僕射、平章事、襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Dahe he left the chancellorship, becoming Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor, prefect of Xiang Prefecture, and Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 828 he left the chancellorship and was appointed Acting Left Vice Director, Grand Councilor, prefect of Xiang, and Shannan East military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，入為左僕射，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered [the capital] as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with charge of the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled as Left Vice Director and given charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十一月，檢校司空、鳳翔尹、鳳翔隴節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was made Acting Minister of Works, Fengxiang Magistrate, and Fengxiang-Long Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, magistrate of Fengxiang, and military commissioner of Fengxiang and Long.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾求還京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on grounds of illness, he requested return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he requested return to the capital on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 七年四月卒，贈司徒，謚曰恭惠。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year he died; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education, posthumous title Gonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the seventh year and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Education with the posthumous title Gonghui (Respectful and Gracious).

sentences.zh: 易直自入仕十年余，常居散秩，不應請辟；

translations.literal: From his entry into office for more than ten years Yizhi often held unassigned rank and did not accept invitations to serve;
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years after entering office Yizhi often held unassigned rank and declined invitations to serve;

sentences.zh: 及居方任，亦以公廉聞。

translations.literal: when he held regional posts he was also known for fairness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: when he held regional posts he was likewise known for fairness and integrity.

sentences.zh: 在相位，未嘗論用親黨，凡於公舉，即無所避。

translations.literal: In the chancellorship he never discussed employing kin or partisans; in all public recommendations he showed no favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: As councilor he never promoted kin or partisans, and in all public recommendations he showed no favoritism.

sentences.zh: 然元和中，吏部尚書鄭餘慶議僕射上日儀制，不與隔品官亢禮。

translations.literal: Yet in the Yuanhe period Minister of Personnel Zheng Yuqing proposed that on the vice directors' first audience day the ritual should not treat them as equal in ceremony with officials of separated rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the Yuanhe reign Minister of Personnel Zheng Yuqing proposed that on a vice director's first audience day he should not exchange equal ceremonial bows with officials of separated rank.

sentences.zh: 易直時為御史中丞，奏駁餘慶所議。

translations.literal: At the time Yizhi was Vice Censor-in-Chief and memorialized in rebuttal of Yuqing's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yizhi was Vice Censor-in-Chief and memorialized in rebuttal of Yuqing's proposal.

sentences.zh: 及易直為左僕射，卻行隔品致敬之禮，時論非之。

translations.literal: When Yizhi became Left Vice Director, he himself performed the separated-rank bowing ceremony, and contemporary opinion criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi became Left Vice Director, he himself performed the separated-rank bowing ceremony, for which contemporaries criticized him.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉李逢吉，字虛舟，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Fengji—Li Fengji, courtesy name Xuzhou, a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji, whose courtesy name was Xuzhou, was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中學士李玄道曾孫。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Academician Li Xuandao of the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Li Xuandao, an academician who served during the Zhenguan period.

sentences.zh: 祖顏，父歸期。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yan; his father was Guiqi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was named Yan, and his father was named Guiqi.

sentences.zh: 逢吉登進士第，釋褐授振武節度掌書記。

translations.literal: Fengji passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office garb he was appointed chief secretary to the Zhenwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji passed the jinshi examination, and upon taking up his first official post he was appointed chief secretary to the Zhenwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入朝為左拾遺、左補闕，改侍御史，充入吐蕃冊命副使、工部員外郎，又充入南詔副使。

translations.literal: He entered court as Left Reminder and Left Supplements Censor, was changed to Attendant Censor, served as deputy envoy for the investiture mission to Tibet and as Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and also served as deputy envoy to Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he served as Left Reminder and Left Supplements Censor before being transferred to Attendant Censor; he then served as deputy envoy on the investiture mission to Tibet while holding the post of Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and later as deputy envoy to Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，使還，拜祠部郎中，轉右司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, on returning from his mission, he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Rites and then transferred to the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: In 809, upon returning from his diplomatic mission, he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Rites and subsequently transferred to the Right Department.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 811 he was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 七年，與司勛員外郎李巨並為太子諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he and Li Ju, Vice Director of the Bureau of Merits, were both appointed tutors to the crown prince and princes.
translations.idiomatic: In 812 he and Li Ju, Vice Director of the Bureau of Merits, were jointly appointed tutors to the crown prince and the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 九年，改中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 814 he was transferred to the post of Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，權知禮部貢舉、騎都尉，賜緋。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year he was given temporary charge of the Ministry of Rites examination and made a Commandant of Cavalry, and was granted the red official robe.
translations.idiomatic: In February 816 he was placed in temporary charge of the civil service examinations under the Ministry of Rites, given the rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and granted the privilege of wearing the red official robe.

sentences.zh: 四月，加朝議大夫、門下侍郎、同平章事，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was further made Senior Grand Master of Discussion, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Associate Grand Counselor, and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: In April he was promoted to Senior Grand Master of Discussion, appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Counselor, and awarded the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 其貢院事，仍委禮部尚書王播署榜。

translations.literal: As for the examination compound affairs, he still entrusted Minister of Rites Wang Bo to post the pass list.
translations.idiomatic: For the examination compound, he still left the posting of the pass list to Wang Bo, the Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 逢吉天與奸回，妒賢傷善。

translations.literal: Fengji was heaven-endowed with treachery and deviousness, jealous of the worthy and injurious to the good.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was naturally treacherous and devious, jealous of the talented and destructive toward the virtuous.

sentences.zh: 時用兵討淮、蔡，憲宗以兵機委裴度，逢吉慮其成功，密沮之，由是相惡。

translations.literal: At the time troops were being used to campaign against Huai and Cai; Xianzong entrusted military planning to Pei Du, and Fengji, fearing his success, secretly obstructed him—thereby the two came to hate each other.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was campaigning against Huai and Cai, Emperor Xianzong entrusted military strategy to Pei Du; Fengji, fearing that Pei would succeed, secretly worked to thwart him, and from that time the two were bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 及度親征，學士令狐楚為度制辭，言不合旨，楚與逢吉相善，帝皆黜之；

translations.literal: When Du personally led the campaign, Academician Linghu Chu drafted a proclamation for Du, but the wording did not accord with the emperor's intent; Chu was on friendly terms with Fengji, and the emperor demoted both;
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du took the field in person, Hanlin Academician Linghu Chu drafted the imperial proclamation on his behalf, but its wording missed the emperor's intent; since Chu was close to Fengji, the emperor demoted both men;

sentences.zh: 罷楚學士，罷逢吉政事，出為劍南東川節度使、檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Chu was removed from his academician post, and Fengji was removed from the administration; Fengji was sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit, with the honorary title of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Chu was stripped of his Hanlin post, and Fengji was removed from the chief ministership and posted out as military commissioner of Jiannan East Circuit, with the honorary title of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，移襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, Fengji was transferred to Prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Muzong came to the throne, Fengji was transferred to serve as Prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 逢吉於帝有侍讀之恩，遣人密結幸臣，求還京師。

translations.literal: Fengji had owed the emperor a debt of gratitude from his service as tutor; he sent men to secretly cultivate favored officials and seek a return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Having once served as Muzong's tutor, Fengji owed the emperor a personal debt; he secretly cultivated the emperor's favorites in hopes of being recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年三月，召為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Changqing, he was summoned as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In March 822 he was recalled to the capital and appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時裴度亦自太原入朝。

translations.literal: At the time Pei Du also entered court from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Pei Du also arrived at court from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以度招懷河朔功，復留度，與工部侍郎元稹相次拜平章事。

translations.literal: Because of Du's achievements in winning over the Hebei region, Du was kept on, and he and Yuan Zhen, Vice Minister of Works, were in succession appointed Grand Counselors.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Pei Du's success in winning over the Hebei frontier, the court kept him in the capital; he and Yuan Zhen, Vice Minister of Works, were appointed Grand Counselors in quick succession.

sentences.zh: 度在太原時，嘗上表論稹奸邪。

translations.literal: When Du was at Taiyuan, he had once submitted a memorial denouncing Yuan Zhen as treacherous and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at Taiyuan, Pei Du had submitted a memorial accusing Yuan Zhen of treachery and wickedness.

sentences.zh: 及同居相位，逢吉以為勢必相傾，乃遣人告和王傅于方結客，欲為元稹刺裴度。

translations.literal: When they held office together as chief ministers, Fengji believed they would inevitably overthrow each other; he therefore sent someone to report that Tutor of the Heir Apparent Yu Fang was gathering clients, intending to have Yuan Zhen assassinate Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pei Du and Yuan Zhen shared the chief ministership, Fengji expected them to destroy one another; he secretly reported that Yu Fang, Tutor of the Heir Apparent, was gathering swordsmen with the intent of having Yuan Zhen arrange the assassination of Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 及捕于方，鞫之無狀，稹、度俱罷相位，逢吉代度為門下侍郎平章事。

translations.literal: When Yu Fang was arrested and interrogated with nothing substantiated, both Yuan Zhen and Pei Du were removed from the chief ministership; Fengji replaced Du as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Fang was arrested and interrogated, no proof emerged; both Yuan Zhen and Pei Du were stripped of their chief ministerships, and Fengji replaced Pei Du as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 自是浸以恩澤結朝臣之不逞者，造作謗言，百端中傷裴度。

translations.literal: From then on he gradually used favors to win over unruly court officials, fabricating slanders of every sort to wound Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he steadily cultivated discontented officials with favors, fabricating slanders of every kind to undermine Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 賴學士李紳、韋處厚等顯於上前，言度為逢吉排斥，而度於國有功，不宜擯棄，故得以僕射在朝。

translations.literal: Thanks to Academicians Li Shen and Wei Chuhou, who spoke plainly before the emperor, saying Du had been driven out by Fengji yet had rendered great service to the state and should not be cast aside, Du was thus able to remain at court as a Director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Hanlin Academicians Li Shen and Wei Chuhou, who spoke openly before the throne, arguing that Pei Du had been driven out by Fengji despite his great service to the state and ought not be discarded, Pei Du was allowed to remain at court with the title of Director of the Department.

sentences.zh: 時已失河朔，而王智興擅據徐州，李㝏據汴州。

translations.literal: At the time the Hebei region had already been lost, while Wang Zhixing arbitrarily held Xuzhou and Li Tong held Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had lost control of the Hebei frontier; Wang Zhixing had seized Xuzhou on his own authority, and Li Tong held Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 國威不振，天下延頸俟度再秉國鈞，以攘暴亂。

translations.literal: The state's authority did not flourish; all under Heaven stretched their necks awaiting Du's again holding the nation's helm to sweep away violent disorder.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige had collapsed; the whole empire looked to Pei Du to take up the reins of government once again and put down the rampant disorder.

sentences.zh: 及為逢吉嫁禍，奪其權，四海為之側目，朝士上疏論列者十餘人。

translations.literal: When he was made the victim of Fengji's frame-up and stripped of power, the four seas looked on with alarm, and more than ten court officials submitted memorials enumerating the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengji framed him and stripped him of power, the whole empire looked on in dismay, and more than ten court officials submitted memorials protesting the injustice.

sentences.zh: 屬時君荒淫，政出群小，而度竟逐外籓。

translations.literal: It happened that the ruler of the time was debauched and dissolute, government issued from a clique of petty men, and in the end Du was expelled to an outer province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was dissolute, power had passed to petty favorites, and in the end Pei Du was banished to a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 學士李紳有寵，逢吉惡之，乃除為中丞，又欲出於外。

translations.literal: Academician Li Shen had the emperor's favor; Fengji hated him and therefore appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief, intending also to send him outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The favored Hanlin Academician Li Shen aroused Fengji's hatred; Fengji had him appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief with the further aim of posting him outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃以吏部侍郎韓愈為京兆尹，兼御史大夫，放臺參。

translations.literal: He therefore made Han Yu, Vice Minister of Personnel, Prefect of the Capital and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, releasing the right of yamen inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Han Yu, Vice Minister of Personnel, as Prefect of the Capital and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, granting him the right to conduct formal yamen inspections.

sentences.zh: 以紳褊直，必與愈爭。

translations.literal: Because Shen was narrow and blunt, he would surely clash with Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Calculating that the rigid and blunt Li Shen would inevitably come into conflict with Han Yu,

sentences.zh: 及制出，紳果移牒往來。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Shen indeed exchanged official communications back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: when the appointment was announced, Li Shen immediately began exchanging official dispatches with Han Yu.

sentences.zh: 愈性木強，遂至語辭不遜，喧論於朝。

translations.literal: Han Yu's nature was stubborn and unyielding, and matters reached the point of disrespectful words, causing a clamor of dispute at court.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu's temperament was stubborn and inflexible, and the quarrel escalated to open discourtesy, creating a public uproar at court.

sentences.zh: 逢吉乃罷愈為兵部侍郎，紳為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Fengji then removed Han Yu to Vice Minister of War and sent Shen out as Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji then demoted Han Yu to Vice Minister of War and posted Li Shen out as Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 紳中謝日，帝留而不遣。

translations.literal: On the day Shen offered thanks in mid-court, the emperor retained him and did not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shen came to court to offer thanks for his appointment, the emperor kept him in the capital and refused to let him depart.

sentences.zh: 翼城人鄭註以醫藥得幸於中尉王守澄，逢吉令其從子仲言賂註，求結於守澄。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu of Yicheng, through medicine, won the favor of Eunuch Commander Wang Shoucheng; Fengji had his nephew Zhongyan bribe Zhu to seek connection with Shoucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu of Yicheng had won Wang Shoucheng's favor through his medical skills; Fengji had his nephew Zhongyan bribe Zhu in order to cultivate Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 仲言辯譎多端，守澄見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was eloquent, devious, and multifaceted; Shoucheng was greatly pleased when he met him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was eloquent and scheming in many ways; Shoucheng took an immediate liking to him.

sentences.zh: 自是，逢吉有助，事無違者。

translations.literal: From then on, with Fengji having assistance, in affairs nothing went against him.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on Fengji had powerful backing, and nothing he wanted was denied.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初即位，年方童丱，守澄從容奏曰：「陛下得為太子，逢吉之力也。

translations.literal: When Jingzong had just acceded, still a child, Shoucheng calmly memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty's becoming crown prince was due to Fengji's power.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong first acceded to the throne, still little more than a boy, Shoucheng remarked to the emperor at leisure: "Your Majesty owes your position as crown prince to Li Fengji's efforts.

sentences.zh: 是時，杜元穎、李紳堅請立深王為太子。」

translations.literal: At that time Du Yuanying and Li Shen had firmly pleaded to install Prince Shen as crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du Yuanying and Li Shen had vigorously argued for making Prince Shen the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 乃貶紳端州司馬。

translations.literal: Li Shen was then demoted to Magistrate of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen was accordingly demoted to Magistrate of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝士代逢吉鳴吠者，張又新、李續之、張權輿、劉棲楚、李虞、程昔範、姜洽、李仲言，時號「八關十六子」。

translations.literal: Court officials who barked on Fengji's behalf included Zhang Youxin, Li Xuzhi, Zhang Quanyu, Liu Qichu, Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, Jiang Qia, and Li Zhongyan—at the time called "the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."
translations.idiomatic: The court officials who served as Fengji's barkers included Zhang Youxin, Li Xuzhi, Zhang Quanyu, Liu Qichu, Li Yu, Cheng Xifan, Jiang Qia, and Li Zhongyan; they were known at the time as "the Eight Passes and Sixteen Sons."

sentences.zh: 又新等八人居要劇，而胥附者又八人，有求於逢吉者，必先經此八人納賂，無不如意者。

translations.literal: The eight men headed by Youxin held important and urgent posts, and those who attached themselves to them numbered eight more; anyone who had requests of Fengji had first to pay bribes through these eight—nothing failed to go as wished.
translations.idiomatic: The eight, led by Zhang Youxin, held key posts, and eight more hangers-on clustered around them; anyone seeking Fengji's favor had first to pay bribes through these eight men, and no request went unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 逢吉尋封涼國公，邑千戶，兼右僕射。

translations.literal: Before long Fengji was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with a fief of one thousand households, and also made Right Director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was soon enfeoffed as Duke of Liang with a fief of one thousand households and appointed Right Director of the Department as well.

sentences.zh: 昭湣即位，左右屢言裴度之賢，曾立大勛，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When Zhaomin acceded, those around him repeatedly spoke of Pei Du's worth and his once having achieved great merit; the emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaomin came to the throne, his attendants repeatedly praised Pei Du's virtues and his great earlier achievements, and the emperor was much impressed.

sentences.zh: 因中使往興元，即令問訊。

translations.literal: Accordingly a palace envoy was sent to Xingyuan and ordered to convey inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accordingly dispatched a palace envoy to Xingyuan to convey his regards.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，度連上章請入覲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli, Du repeatedly submitted memorials requesting permission to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoli reign, Pei Du repeatedly petitioned for permission to return to court.

sentences.zh: 逢吉之黨坐不安席，如矢攢身，乃相與為謀，欲沮其來。

translations.literal: Fengji's faction could not sit at ease, as if arrows pierced their bodies; they therefore plotted together, intending to obstruct his coming.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji's faction could not sit still—they felt as if arrows were piercing their bodies—and they plotted together to block Pei Du's return.

sentences.zh: 張權輿撰「非衣小兒」之謠，傳於閭巷。

translations.literal: Zhang Quanyu composed the ballad "the feiyi child," and it spread through lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quanyu composed a street ballad about "the not-clothed child," which spread through the neighborhoods.

sentences.zh: 言度相有天分，應謠讖。

translations.literal: It said Du as minister had the mandate of Heaven and accorded with the ballad's omen.
translations.idiomatic: The ballad claimed that Pei Du as chief minister had a Heaven-granted destiny and fulfilled its prophetic omen.

sentences.zh: 而韋處厚於上前解析，言權輿所撰之言。

translations.literal: But Wei Chuhou explained before the emperor, saying these were words Zhang Quanyu had composed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou, however, explained before the throne that the ballad was Zhang Quanyu's own fabrication.

sentences.zh: 既不能沮，又令衛尉卿劉遵古從人安再榮告武昭謀害逢吉。

translations.literal: When they could not obstruct him thus, they also had Commandant of the Guard Liu Zungu employ his follower An Zairong to report that Wu Zhao plotted to kill Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: When that failed to stop Pei Du, they had Liu Zungu, Commandant of the Guard, use his follower An Zairong to accuse Wu Zhao of plotting to assassinate Fengji.

sentences.zh: 武昭者，有才力，裴度破淮、蔡時獎用之，累奏為刺史。

translations.literal: Wu Zhao possessed talent and strength; when Pei Du broke Huai and Cai, Du praised and employed him and repeatedly recommended him for prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhao was a man of ability and force; when Pei Du conquered Huai and Cai, Pei had taken him under his wing and repeatedly recommended him for prefectural posts.

sentences.zh: 及度被斥，昭以門吏久不見用，客於京師，途窮頗有怨言。

translations.literal: When Du was driven out, Zhao, long unused as a retainer, stayed as a guest in the capital; destitute on the road, he had many resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Du's dismissal, Zhao, who had long served as a retainer but received no appointment, lingered in the capital; impoverished and frustrated, he voiced considerable resentment.

sentences.zh: 逢吉冀法司鞫昭行止，則顯裴度任用，以沮入朝之行。

translations.literal: Fengji hoped the judicial office would interrogate Zhao's conduct, thereby exposing Pei Du's employment of him, to obstruct the journey to court.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji hoped that if the judicial authorities interrogated Wu Zhao, Pei Du's past patronage of him would be exposed and Pei Du's return to court could be blocked.

sentences.zh: 逢吉又與同列李程不協。

translations.literal: Fengji also did not get along with his fellow minister Li Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was also at odds with his fellow chief minister Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 太學博士李涉、金吾兵曹茅匯者，於京師貴遊間以氣俠相許，二人出入程及逢吉之門。

translations.literal: Li She, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and Mao Hui, militia officer of the Gold Crow Guard, were mutually pledged in chivalrous spirit among the capital's noble wanderers; the two came and went at the gates of both Cheng and Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Li She, an Erudite of the Imperial Academy, and Mao Hui, a militia officer of the Gold Crow Guard, moved in the chivalrous circles of the capital's elite; both frequented the households of Li Cheng and Li Fengji.

sentences.zh: 水部郎中李仍叔，程之族，知武昭郁郁恨不得官，仍叔謂昭曰：「程欲與公官，但逢吉阻之。」

translations.literal: Li Rengshu, Director of the Bureau of Waterways, a kinsman of Cheng, knew Wu Zhao was depressed and resentful at failing to obtain an office; Rengshu said to Zhao: "Cheng wishes to give you an office, but Fengji obstructs it."
translations.idiomatic: Li Rengshu, Director of the Bureau of Waterways and a kinsman of Li Cheng, knew that Wu Zhao was dejected over his failure to obtain a post; Rengshu told Zhao: "Li Cheng wants to give you an appointment, but Li Fengji is blocking it."

sentences.zh: 昭愈憤怒，因酒與京師人劉審、張少騰說刺逢吉之言。

translations.literal: Zhao grew yet more furious; under the influence of wine he spoke with the capital men Liu Shen and Zhang Shaoteng of assassinating Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhao grew even angrier, and while drunk he discussed assassinating Fengji with two men of the capital, Liu Shen and Zhang Shaoteng.

sentences.zh: 審以昭言告張權輿，乃聞於逢吉，即令茅匯召昭相見，逢吉厚相結托，自是疑怨之言稍息。

translations.literal: Shen reported Zhao's words to Zhang Quanyu, and it reached Fengji; Fengji immediately had Mao Hui summon Zhao to meet him, and Fengji bound him closely in trust—thereafter words of suspicion and resentment gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen reported Wu Zhao's words to Zhang Quanyu, and the matter reached Fengji; Fengji had Mao Hui summon Wu Zhao, treated him with great favor, and won his loyalty—after which talk of suspicion and resentment gradually died down.

sentences.zh: 逢吉待茅匯尤厚，嘗與匯書云：「足下當字僕為『自求』，僕當字足下為『利見』」。

translations.literal: Fengji treated Mao Hui with especial favor; he once wrote to Hui: "You should style me 'self-seeking'; I shall style you 'profit seen.'"
translations.idiomatic: Fengji showed Mao Hui particular favor; in one letter he wrote: "You should address me as 'Self-Seeking'; I shall address you as 'Profit Seen.'"

sentences.zh: 文字往來，其間甚密。

translations.literal: Letters went back and forth; the intimacy between them was very close.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged letters frequently, and their intimacy was very close.

sentences.zh: 及裴度求覲，無計沮之，即令訐武昭事，以暴揚其跡。

translations.literal: When Pei Du requested an audience visit, having no plan to obstruct it, he immediately had the Wu Zhao affair denounced, to expose and publicize the trail.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du petitioned to come to court and they had no further means to stop him, they denounced the Wu Zhao affair to expose the whole trail of connections.

sentences.zh: 再榮既告，李仲言誡匯曰：「言武昭與李程同謀則活，否則爾死。」

translations.literal: After Zairong had reported, Li Zhongyan warned Hui: "Say Wu Zhao and Li Cheng conspired together and you live; otherwise you die."
translations.idiomatic: After An Zairong made his accusation, Li Zhongyan warned Mao Hui: "If you say Wu Zhao and Li Cheng plotted together, you will live; otherwise you will die."

sentences.zh: 匯曰：「冤死甘心。

translations.literal: Hui said: "To die wronged—I accept it willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hui replied: "I would willingly die wronged.

sentences.zh: 誣人以自免，予不為也。」

translations.literal: To falsely accuse others to save oneself—I will not do it."
translations.idiomatic: I will not falsely accuse others to save myself."

sentences.zh: 及昭下獄，逢吉之醜跡皆彰。

translations.literal: When Zhao was imprisoned, all of Fengji's ugly tracks were exposed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zhao was thrown into prison, all of Fengji's sordid scheming came to light.

sentences.zh: 昭死，仲言流象州，茅匯流巂州，李涉流康州，李虞自拾遺為河南士曹。

translations.literal: Zhao died; Zhongyan was banished to Xiangzhou, Mao Hui to Suizhou, Li She to Kangzhou, and Li Yu was reduced from Reminder to Senior Clerk of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhao was executed; Li Zhongyan was exiled to Xiang Prefecture, Mao Hui to Su Prefecture, and Li She to Kang Prefecture; Li Yu was demoted from Reminder to Senior Clerk of Henan.

sentences.zh: 敬宗待裴度益厚，乃自漢中召還，復知政事。

translations.literal: Jingzong treated Pei Du with increasing favor; he was therefore recalled from Hanzhong and again given charge of the administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong treated Pei Du with ever greater favor, recalled him from Hanzhong, and restored him to the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 逢吉檢校司空、平章事、襄州刺史、山南東道節度使，仍請張又新、李續之為參佐。

translations.literal: Fengji was made Honorary Grand Marshal, Grand Counselor, Prefect of Xiangzhou, and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and still requested Zhang Youxin and Li Xuzhi as staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was appointed Honorary Grand Marshal and Grand Counselor, posted as Prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and took Zhang Youxin and Li Xuzhi with him as staff officers.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，改汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he was changed to Prefect of Bianzhou and military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 828 he was transferred to serve as Prefect of Bianzhou and military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，入為太子太師、東都留守、東畿汝防禦使，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year he entered court as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, Guardian of the Eastern Capital, Commissioner for the Defense of the Eastern Capital Circuit and Ru Region, with the added rank of Grand Master with Equipage equal to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In August 831 he was recalled to serve as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, Guardian of the Eastern Capital, and Commissioner for the Defense of the Eastern Capital and Ru regions, with the added honorific rank of Grand Master with Equipage equal to the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 八年，李訓用事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Li Xun wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: In 834 Li Xun came to power.

sentences.zh: 三月，徵拜左僕射，兼守司徒。

translations.literal: In the third month he was summoned and appointed Left Director of the Department, concurrently retaining the post of Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In March he was summoned and appointed Left Director of the Department while retaining the post of Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 時逢吉已老，病足，不任朝謁，即以司徒致仕。

translations.literal: At the time Fengji was already old, his feet afflicted with illness, unable to undertake court attendance; he therefore retired with the title of Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: By then Fengji was elderly and crippled by foot ailments, unable to attend court; he retired with the title of Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 九年正月卒，時年七十八。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he died, aged seventy-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of 835, at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant, with posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant and given the posthumous epithet Cheng.

sentences.zh: 段文昌段文昌，字墨卿，西河人。

translations.literal: Duan Wenchang—Duan Wenchang, courtesy name Moqing, a native of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchang, whose courtesy name was Moqing, was a native of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 高祖志玄，陪葬昭陵，圖形凌煙閣。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Zhixuan was buried at Zhaoling as an attendant to the tomb, and his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His distinguished ancestor Duan Zhixuan was buried at Zhaoling in attendance upon the imperial tomb, and his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 祖德皎，贈給事中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dejiao was posthumously made Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dejiao was posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 父諤，循州刺史，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: His father E was Prefect of Xunzhou and was posthumously made Left Director of the Department.
translations.idiomatic: His father E had served as Prefect of Xun Prefecture and was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Director of the Department.

sentences.zh: 文昌家於荊州，倜儻有氣義，節度使裴胄知之而不能用。

translations.literal: Wenchang made his home in Jingzhou; he was free and easy, with chivalrous spirit; Military Commissioner Pei Zhou knew him but could not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang made his home in Jingzhou; he was bold and generous, a man of honor; the military commissioner Pei Zhou recognized his talent but could not find a place for him.

sentences.zh: 韋臯在蜀，表授校書郎。

translations.literal: When Wei Gao was in Shu, he memorialized and granted him the post of Collator.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Gao governed Shu, he recommended Wenchang and had him appointed Collator.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫刺忠州，文昌嘗以文幹之。

translations.literal: When Li Jifu was prefect of Zhongzhou, Wenchang once presented his writings to gain his notice.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu served as prefect of Zhong Prefecture, Wenchang had once sought his patronage by presenting his writings.

sentences.zh: 及吉甫居相位，與裴垍同加獎擢，授登封尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: When Jifu held the chief ministership, he and Pei Ji together further praised and promoted him, appointing him Commandant of Dengfeng and Collator at the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu rose to the chief ministership, he and Pei Ji jointly recommended Wenchang for advancement, appointing him Commandant of Dengfeng and Collator at the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 俄拜監察御史，遷補闕，改祠部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Investigating Censor, was promoted to Supplements Censor, and was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Investigating Censor, promoted to Supplements Censor, and transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Rites.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年，守本官，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe, retaining his original post, he served as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 816, while retaining his existing post, he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 文昌，武元衡之子婿也。

translations.literal: Wenchang was the son-in-law of Wu Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang was the son-in-law of Wu Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 元衡與宰相韋貫之不協，憲宗欲召文昌為學士，貫之奏曰：「文昌志尚不修，不可擢居近密。」

translations.literal: Yuanheng was not on good terms with Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi; Xianzong wished to summon Wenchang as academician, and Guanzhi memorialized: "Wenchang's aspirations and conduct are not cultivated; he cannot be promoted to close and confidential service."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanheng was at odds with Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi; when Emperor Xianzong wished to appoint Wenchang Hanlin Academician, Guanzhi memorialized: "Wenchang's character is unreformed; he is unfit for promotion to the inner circle of the throne."

sentences.zh: 至是貫之罷相，李逢吉乃用文昌為學士，轉祠部郎中，賜緋，依前充職。

translations.literal: At this time Guanzhi was removed from the chief ministership, and Li Fengji then employed Wenchang as academician, transferred him to Director of the Bureau of Rites, granted him the red robe, and he continued in his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Guanzhi had been removed from office, and Li Fengji appointed Wenchang Hanlin Academician, promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Rites, granted him the red robe, and left him in his previous post.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加知制誥。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was further given charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 819 he was additionally assigned to draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 十五年，穆宗即位，正拜中書舍人，尋拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Muzong acceded; Wenchang was formally appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, and soon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In 820, when Muzong came to the throne, Wenchang was formally appointed Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and soon afterward Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，拜章請退。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In 821 he submitted a memorial requesting to step down from office.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以文昌少在西蜀，詔授西川節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The court, because Wenchang had spent his youth in western Shu, issued an edict appointing him military commissioner of Xichuan and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenchang had spent his youth in western Shu, the court appointed him military commissioner of Xichuan and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 文昌素洽蜀人之情，至是以寬政為治，嚴靜有斷，蠻夷畏服。

translations.literal: Wenchang had long been in accord with the feelings of the people of Shu; upon arrival he governed with lenient policy, stern yet calm in decision, and the barbarians feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang had long understood the temperament of the people of Shu; once in office he governed with a lenient hand, combining firm discipline with calm decisiveness, and the frontier tribes submitted to his authority.

sentences.zh: 二年，雲南入寇，黔中觀察使崔元略上言，朝廷憂之，乃詔文昌禦備。

translations.literal: In the second year Yunnan invaded; Cui Yuanlue, Commissioner of Qianzhong, submitted a memorial; the court was alarmed and ordered Wenchang to prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In 822 Yunnan launched an invasion; Cui Yuanlue, Commissioner of Qianzhong, reported it to the throne; alarmed, the court ordered Wenchang to prepare the defenses.

sentences.zh: 文昌走一介之使以喻之，蠻寇即退。

translations.literal: Wenchang sent a single envoy to instruct them, and the barbarian invaders immediately withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang dispatched a lone messenger to reason with them, and the invaders immediately withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，征拜邢部尚書，轉兵部，兼判左丞事。

translations.literal: When Jingzong acceded, he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Xing Department (the text reads 邢 but almost certainly intends 刑, the Ministry of Justice); he was then transferred to the Ministry of War and concurrently given charge of the Left Vice Director's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzong came to the throne, Wenchang was summoned and appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the Ministry of War while concurrently handling the duties of the Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，遷御史大夫，尋檢校尚書右僕射、揚州大都督府長史、同平章事、淮南節度使。

translations.literal: When Wenzong acceded, he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; soon he was made acting Right Director of the Department, Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, Associate Chief Minister, and Military Commissioner of Huainan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Wenchang was promoted to Censor-in-Chief; soon he was provisionally appointed Right Director of the Department, Chief Administrator of Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, Associate Chief Minister, and Military Commissioner of Huainan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，移鎮荊南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, he was transferred to command Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 830 he was transferred to take command of Jingnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 文昌於荊、蜀皆有先祖故第，至是贖為浮圖祠。

translations.literal: Wenchang had ancestral old mansions in both Jing and Shu; at this time he redeemed them and made them Buddhist temple shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang owned ancestral family mansions in both Jing and Shu; he now reclaimed them and converted them into Buddhist shrines.

sentences.zh: 又以先人墳墓在荊州，別營居第，以置祖禰影堂，歲時伏臘，良辰美景享薦之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because his forebears' graves were in Jingzhou, he separately built a residence to set up memorial halls for his ancestors and forefathers, and at the seasonal festivals of summer and winter solstice, on fine days and beautiful scenery, he offered sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because his ancestors' tombs were in Jing Prefecture, he built a separate residence there, outfitting it with memorial halls for his forebears; at the midsummer and midwinter sacrifices, and whenever the season was fair, he would offer oblations.

sentences.zh: 徹祭，即以音聲歌舞繼之，如事生者，搢紳非焉。

translations.literal: When the sacrificial rites ended, he immediately followed with music, singing, and dancing, as if serving the living; the gentry condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the rites were complete, he would have music and dancers perform, treating the dead as though they were still alive—a practice the officials deplored.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為劍南西川節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he again became Military Commissioner of Western Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In 832 he was once again appointed Military Commissioner of Western Chuan in Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，賜春衣中使至，受宣畢，無疾而卒，年六十三，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, the imperial envoy bringing spring garments arrived; when he had received the edict, he died without illness, aged sixty-three; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 835, when the palace envoy arrived bearing the emperor's gift of spring robes and Wenchang had received the imperial message, he died suddenly without prior illness, at the age of sixty-three. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 文昌布素之時，所向不偶。

translations.literal: When Wenchang was in plain cloth, wherever he turned he met no fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days as a commoner, nothing ever seemed to go Wenchang's way.

sentences.zh: 及其達也，揚歷顯重，出入將相，洎二十年。

translations.literal: When he achieved advancement, he rose through prominent and weighty offices, entering and leaving the ranks of generals and chief ministers, until nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rose to power, he held one prestigious post after another, moving between the highest civil and military offices for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 其服飾玩好、歌童妓女，茍悅於心，無所愛惜，乃至奢侈過度，物議貶之。

translations.literal: For clothing and ornaments, curios and pleasures, singing boys and courtesans—whatever pleased his heart—he spared nothing, even to excess luxury; public opinion condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Fine clothes, curios, singing boys, and courtesans—whatever gratified him, he lavished money on without restraint, until his extravagance became notorious and invited public censure.

sentences.zh: 子成式。

translations.literal: His son was Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 成式，字柯古，以廕入官，為秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Chengshi, courtesy name Kegu, entered office by yin privilege and served as Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshi, whose courtesy name was Kegu, entered government service by inherited privilege and was appointed Collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 研精苦學，秘閣書籍，披閱皆遍。

translations.literal: He delved into study with exhausting diligence; of the Secret Pavilion's books and records, he read through them all.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to rigorous study and read every book in the Secret Pavilion collection.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong, he went out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantong era he was posted as Prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 解印，寓居襄陽，以閑放自適。

translations.literal: He surrendered his seal, took up residence in Xiangyang, and found contentment in leisurely freedom.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office he settled in Xiangyang, content to live in leisurely retirement.

sentences.zh: 家多書史，用以自娛，尤深於佛書。

translations.literal: His home had many books and histories, which he used for self-amusement; he was especially deep in Buddhist texts.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a large library at home for his own amusement and was especially learned in Buddhist literature.

sentences.zh: 所著《酉陽雜俎》傳於時。

translations.literal: His work Miscellaneous Morsels from Youyang circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: His Miscellaneous Morsels from Youyang enjoyed wide circulation in his day.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫宋申錫，字慶臣。

translations.literal: Song Shenxi—Song Shenxi, courtesy name Qingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shenxi, whose courtesy name was Qingchen.

sentences.zh: 祖素，父叔夜。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Su; his father was Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Su and his father was Shuye.

sentences.zh: 申錫少孤貧，有文學。

translations.literal: Shenxi was orphaned young and poor, but had literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi lost his father early and grew up in poverty, yet he possessed genuine literary talent.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，釋褐秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and, upon doffing his commoner's garb, was made Collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and, upon entering service, was appointed Collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韋貫之罷相，出湖南，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Wei Guanzhi was removed as chief minister and went out to Hunan, he recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Guanzhi was dismissed from the chief ministership and posted to Hunan, he recruited Shenxi as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 其後累佐使府。

translations.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly served as aide in commissioners' offices.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve on several successive commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Drafting Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: In 822 he was promoted to Drafting Recorder.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，轉禮部員外郎，尋充翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli, he was changed to Vice Director of the Bureau of Rites, and soon served as Hanlin Lecturer Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 826 he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Rites and soon after appointed Hanlin Lecturer Academician.

sentences.zh: 申錫始自策名，及在朝行，清慎介潔，不趨黨與。

translations.literal: From the time Shenxi first made his name and while he was in court ranks, he was pure, cautious, upright, and clean, and did not rush toward faction and clique.
translations.idiomatic: From his first official appointment onward, and throughout his service at court, Shenxi was scrupulous, cautious, and incorruptible, and he kept aloof from factional alignments.

sentences.zh: 當長慶、寶歷之間，時風囂薄，朋比大扇。

translations.literal: During the period between Changqing and Baoli, the temper of the age was clamorous and shallow, and factional comparison spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changqing and Baoli reigns, the political atmosphere was cynical and coarse, and partisan factionalism ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 及申錫被用，時論以為激勸。

translations.literal: When Shenxi was employed, contemporary opinion regarded it as encouragement and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenxi was brought into office, public opinion took his appointment as a signal to encourage rectitude and restrain corruption.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，拜戶部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Wenzong acceded, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue and charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, Shenxi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue and charged with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，正拜中書舍人，復為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter and again served as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In 828 he was formally appointed Secretariat Drafter and reappointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 初，文宗常患中人權柄太盛，自元和、寶歷，比致宮禁之禍。

translations.literal: At first, Wenzong often worried that eunuchs' power and authority were too great; since Yuanhe and Baoli, this had repeatedly brought calamity within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had long been troubled by the eunuchs' excessive power; ever since the Yuanhe and Baoli reigns, their dominance had repeatedly brought disaster upon the inner court.

sentences.zh: 及王守澄之領禁兵，恃其宿舊，跋扈尤甚。

translations.literal: When Wang Shoucheng took command of the palace armies, relying on his long-standing ties, he was especially overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Shoucheng took command of the palace guard, he leaned on his long-standing influence and became more overbearing than ever.

sentences.zh: 有鄭註者，依恃守澄為奸利，出入禁軍，賣官販權，中外鹹扼腕視之。
