translations.literal: There was one Zheng Zhu, who relied on Shoucheng for villainous profit; entering and leaving the palace armies, selling offices and trafficking in power—all within and without clenched their fists in rage at the sight.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zheng Zhu attached himself to Wang Shoucheng and used that connection for illicit profit, moving freely among the palace troops while buying and selling offices and peddling influence; officials and commoners alike watched in helpless fury.

sentences.zh: 文宗雅知之，不能堪。

translations.literal: Wenzong knew this well and could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong was well aware of all this and found it intolerable.

sentences.zh: 申錫時居內廷，文宗察其忠厚，可任以事。

translations.literal: Shenxi then dwelt in the inner court; Wenzong observed that he was loyal and honest and could be entrusted with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi was then serving in the inner court; the emperor saw that he was steadfast and trustworthy and could be relied upon for important matters.

sentences.zh: 嘗因召對，與申錫從容言及守澄，無可奈何，令與外廷朝臣謀去之，且約命為宰相。

translations.literal: Once, on being summoned for audience, he spoke at ease with Shenxi about Shoucheng; finding himself helpless, he ordered him to join with outer-court ministers to plot Shoucheng's removal, and moreover promised to appoint him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: On one such private audience, the emperor spoke frankly with Shenxi about Wang Shoucheng; finding himself powerless to act alone, he instructed Shenxi to conspire with outer-court ministers to remove him, and pledged to appoint Shenxi chief minister in return.

sentences.zh: 申錫頓首謝之。

translations.literal: Shenxi kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜左丞。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 逾月，加平章事。

translations.literal: After a month, he was added as Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 申錫素能謹直，寵遇超輩，時情大為屬望。

translations.literal: Shenxi had always been able to be careful and upright; his favored treatment surpassed his peers, and public sentiment greatly invested hope in him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi had always been known for his integrity; the exceptional favor shown him raised expectations throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 及到中書，剖斷循常，望實頗不相副。

translations.literal: When he reached the Secretariat, his decisions followed the routine; reputation and reality did not match well.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the chancellorship, however, his handling of affairs proved merely conventional, falling short of what people had hoped for.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，忽降中人召宰相入赴延英。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, suddenly palace eunuchs descended summoning chief ministers to enter and attend at Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 831, palace eunuchs suddenly arrived with orders summoning the chief ministers to Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 路隨、李宗閔、牛僧孺等既至中書東門，中人云：「所召無宋申錫。」

translations.literal: Lu Sui, Li Zongmin, Niu Sengru, and the rest, having reached the east gate of the Secretariat, the eunuch said: "Those summoned do not include Song Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Sui, Li Zongmin, Niu Sengru, and the others reached the east gate of the Secretariat, the eunuch announced: "Song Shenxi is not among those summoned.

sentences.zh: 申錫始知被罪，望延英以笏叩頭而退。

translations.literal: Shenxi then knew he had been charged with crime; he looked toward Yanying Hall, knocked his head with his tally, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi now realized he was under accusation; he faced Yanying Hall, touched his forehead to his ivory tally in obeisance, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 隨等至，文宗以神策軍中尉王守澄所奏，得本軍虞候豆盧著狀，告宋申錫與漳王謀反，隨等相顧愕然。

translations.literal: When Sui and the others arrived, Wenzong, on the basis of the memorial by Wang Shoucheng, Commander of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies, received a report from Army Inspector Dou Luzhu of that army, accusing Song Shenxi and the Prince of Zhang of plotting rebellion; Sui and the others looked at each other in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the others arrived, Emperor Wenzong presented the memorial of Wang Shoucheng, Commander of the Divine Strategy Armies, along with a deposition by the army inspector Dou Luzhu, charging Song Shenxi and the Prince of Zhang with treason. The ministers stared at one another in shock.

sentences.zh: 初，守澄於浴堂以鄭註所構告於文宗，守澄即時於市肆追捕，又將以二百騎就靖恭裏屠申錫之家。

translations.literal: At first, Shoucheng in the bath hall reported to Wenzong the accusation Zheng Zhu had fabricated; Shoucheng immediately sent pursuers into the market stalls, and was also about to take two hundred mounted men to Jinggong Lane to slaughter Shenxi's household.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng had first brought the fabricated accusation to the emperor in the bath hall; he immediately dispatched agents to scour the markets for suspects and was preparing to lead two hundred cavalrymen to Jinggong Lane to massacre Shenxi's entire household.

sentences.zh: 會內官馬存亮同入，諍於文宗曰：「謀反者適宋申錫耳，何不召南司會議。

translations.literal: It happened that the inner official Ma Cunliang entered together, and remonstrated with Wenzong: "The one plotting rebellion is only Song Shenxi—why not summon the Outer Directorate to deliberate together?
translations.idiomatic: The palace official Ma Cunliang happened to enter with them and urgently remonstrated with the emperor: "If the alleged rebel is merely Song Shenxi, why not convene the Outer Directorate for joint deliberation?

sentences.zh: 今卒然如此，京師企足自為亂矣。」

translations.literal: Now if it suddenly proceeds like this, the capital will stand on tiptoe and throw itself into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: If you act this suddenly, the entire capital will panic and descend into disorder of its own accord.

sentences.zh: 守澄不能難，乃止。

translations.literal: Shoucheng could not refute this, and so stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng could offer no rebuttal and halted his plans.

sentences.zh: 乃召三相告之。

translations.literal: Then he summoned the three chief ministers and told them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then summoned the three chief ministers and informed them.

sentences.zh: 又遣右軍差人於申錫宅捕孔目官張全真、家人買子緣信等。

translations.literal: He also sent men from the Right Army to Shenxi's residence to seize Chief Clerk Zhang Quanzhen, household slaves Mai Ziyuan and Xin, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also dispatched agents from the Right Army to Shenxi's residence to arrest Chief Clerk Zhang Quanzhen, the household slaves Mai Ziyuan and Xin, and others.

sentences.zh: 又於十六宅及市肆追捕胥吏，以成其獄。

translations.literal: He also in the Sixteen Residences and market stalls pursued and seized clerks, to complete the case.
translations.idiomatic: Agents were also dispatched to the Sixteen Princely Residences and the market districts to hunt down minor officials, building the case as they went.

sentences.zh: 文宗又召師保、僕射、尚書丞郎、常侍、給事、諫議、舍人、御史中丞、京兆尹、大理卿，同於中書及集賢院參驗其事。

translations.literal: Wenzong also summoned tutors, Directors of Departments, Assistant Directors and Directors in ministries, Regular Attendants, Drafting Attendants, Remonstrance and Review Officials, Drafting Recorders, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, to jointly examine the matter at the Secretariat and Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong also summoned tutors, department directors, vice ministers and bureau directors, regular attendants, drafting attendants, remonstrance officials, drafting recorders, the vice censor-in-chief, the metropolitan prefect, and the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review to examine the case jointly at the Secretariat and the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 翌日，開延英，召宰臣及議事官，帝自詢問。

translations.literal: The next day Yanying was opened; he summoned chief ministers and deliberating officials, and the emperor personally inquired.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor convened an audience at Yanying Hall, summoning the chief ministers and all officials involved in the deliberations, and questioned them personally.

sentences.zh: 左常侍崔玄亮，給事中李固言，諫議大夫王質，補闕盧鈞、舒元褒、羅泰、蔣系、裴休、竇宗直、韋溫，拾遺李群、韋端符、丁居晦、袁都等一十四人，皆伏玉階下奏以申錫獄付外，請不於禁中訊鞫。

translations.literal: Left Regular Attendant Cui Xuanliang, Drafting Attendant Li Guyán, Remonstrance and Review Grand Master Wang Zhi, Supplements Censors Lu Jun, Shu Yuanyao, Luo Tai, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Dou Zongzhi, and Wei Wen, Reminder Censors Li Qun, Wei Duanfu, Ding Juhui, and Yuan Du—fourteen men in all—all prostrated themselves below the jade steps and memorialized that Shenxi's case be turned over to the outer administration, requesting that it not be interrogated within the forbidden inner precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen remonstrance officials—including Cui Xuanliang, Regular Attendant; Li Guyán, Drafting Attendant; Wang Zhi, Remonstrance and Review Grand Master; the Supplements Censors Lu Jun, Shu Yuanyao, Luo Tai, Jiang Xi, Pei Xiu, Dou Zongzhi, and Wei Wen; and the Reminder Censors Li Qun, Wei Duanfu, Ding Juhui, and Yuan Du—all prostrated themselves before the imperial steps and petitioned that Shenxi's case be transferred to the outer administration rather than tried within the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「吾已謀於公卿大僚，卿等且出。」

translations.literal: Wenzong said: "I have already deliberated with the great ministers and high officials; you all may withdraw for now.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong replied: "I have already consulted the senior ministers; you may all withdraw for now.

sentences.zh: 玄亮固言，援引今古，辭理懇切。

translations.literal: Xuanliang firmly spoke, citing past and present, his reasoning earnest and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang persisted, citing precedents from antiquity to the present, his argument measured but impassioned.

sentences.zh: 玄亮泣涕久之，文宗意稍解，貶申錫為右庶子，漳王為巢縣公。

translations.literal: Xuanliang wept for a long time; Wenzong's mood slightly eased, and Shenxi was demoted to Right Companion to the Heir Apparent, while the Prince of Zhang was made Duke of Chaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang wept at length; the emperor's anger softened somewhat, and Shenxi was demoted to Right Companion to the Heir Apparent while the Prince of Zhang was reduced to Duke of Chaoxian.

sentences.zh: 再貶申錫為開州司馬。

translations.literal: Shenxi was demoted again to Military Adjunct of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi was demoted a second time to military adjutant of Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，申錫既得密旨，乃除王璠為京兆尹，以密旨喻之。

translations.literal: At first, once Shenxi had received the secret edict, he appointed Wang Fan Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao and conveyed the secret edict to him.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the emperor's secret instructions, Shenxi appointed Wang Fan metropolitan prefect and explained the secret plan to him.

sentences.zh: 璠不能謀，而註與守澄知之，潛為其備。

translations.literal: Fan could not devise a plan, while Zhu and Shoucheng learned of it and secretly prepared their defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan proved incapable of carrying out the plot, while Zheng Zhu and Wang Shoucheng learned of it and quietly set their countermeasures in place.

sentences.zh: 漳王湊，文宗之愛弟也，賢而有人望。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhang, Cou, was Wenzong's beloved younger brother; he was worthy and had the people's regard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cou of Zhang was Emperor Wenzong's beloved younger brother—a man of talent held in high public regard.

sentences.zh: 豆盧著者，職屬禁軍，與註親表。

translations.literal: Dou Luzhu's post belonged to the palace armies; he was a close kinsman by marriage to Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luzhu held a post in the palace guard and was a kinsman of Zheng Zhu by marriage.

sentences.zh: 文宗不省其詐，乃罷申錫為庶子。

translations.literal: Wenzong did not perceive the fraud, and so removed Shenxi to be Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong failed to see through the deception and demoted Shenxi to Right Companion to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時京城恟々，眾庶嘩言，以為宰相真連十宅謀反，百僚震駭。

translations.literal: At the time the capital was in uproar; the common people clamored, believing the chief minister truly linked the Ten Residences in plotting rebellion; the hundred officials were shaken in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was in uproar; the populace clamored that the chief minister had genuinely conspired with the princely residences in treason, and officials throughout the court were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 居一二日，方審其詐。

translations.literal: After one or two days, they finally verified it was fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a day or two did people realize the charge was fabricated.

sentences.zh: 諫官伏閣懇論，文宗震怒，叱諫官令出者數四。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials prostrated themselves at the gate and pleaded earnestly; Wenzong was enraged and shouted at remonstrance officials to leave, several times four.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials petitioned at the palace gate with urgent appeals; Emperor Wenzong flew into a rage and repeatedly ordered them to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 時中外屬望大僚三數人廷辯其事。

translations.literal: At the time within and without, hope rested on three or so great officials to debate the matter in court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, officials throughout the empire looked to several senior ministers to argue the case openly at court.

sentences.zh: 僕射竇易直曰：「人臣無將，將而必誅。」

translations.literal: Director of Department Dou Yizhi said: "A minister must not harbor rebellion; if he does, he must be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yizhi, Director of the Department, declared: "No subject may harbor rebellious intent; whoever does must be executed.

sentences.zh: 聞者愕然。

translations.literal: Those who heard were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him were stunned.

sentences.zh: 唯京兆尹崔琯、大理卿王正雅連上疏請出內獄，且曰：「王師文未獲，即獄未具，請出豆盧著與申錫同付外廷勘。」

translations.literal: Only Metropolitan Prefect Cui Guan and Chief Judge Wang Zhengya repeatedly submitted memorials requesting release from the inner prison, and moreover said: "Wang Shiwen has not yet been captured; that is, the case is not yet complete—request that Dou Luzhu and Shenxi alike be turned over together to the outer court for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Only the metropolitan prefect Cui Guan and the chief judge Wang Zhengya submitted repeated memorials calling for the case to be moved out of the inner prison, arguing: "Wang Shiwen has not yet been arrested, so the case remains incomplete—we ask that Dou Luzhu be handed over along with Shenxi to the outer court for a joint investigation.

sentences.zh: 當時人情翕然推重。

translations.literal: Popular sentiment at the time unanimously honored them.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion at once rallied behind them in admiration.

sentences.zh: 初議申錫抵死，顧物論不可，又將投於嶺表。

translations.literal: At first they deliberated that Shenxi should die for the offense; but considering public opinion would not accept this, they next proposed sending him to the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The initial plan was to execute Shenxi, but prevailing opinion would not allow it; the court then considered banishing him to the far south.

sentences.zh: 文宗終悟外廷之言，乃有開州之命。

translations.literal: Wenzong finally understood the words of the outer court, and so there came the appointment to Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong finally heeded the outer court's counsel and issued the order posting Shenxi to Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，申錫既被罪，怡然不以為意，自中書歸私第，止於外廳，素服以俟命。

translations.literal: At first, once Shenxi had been charged, he was at ease and did not take it to heart; from the Secretariat he returned to his private residence, stopping in the outer hall, in plain robes awaiting his fate.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenxi first learned of the accusation, he remained composed; he left the Secretariat for his home, waited in the outer hall in undyed robes, and calmly awaited the emperor's decree.

sentences.zh: 其妻出謂之曰：「公為宰相，人臣位極於此，何負天子反乎？」

translations.literal: His wife came out and said to him: "You served as chief minister; a minister's position reaches its extreme at this—what debt to the Son of Heaven would make you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: His wife came to him and said: "You rose to the chancellorship—the highest station any subject can reach. What could you possibly owe the emperor that would drive you to treason?

sentences.zh: 申錫曰：「吾生被厚恩，擢相位，不能鋤去奸亂，反為所羅織，夫人察申錫，豈反者乎？」

translations.literal: Shenxi said: "I have received thick favor all my life, was raised to the chief ministership, yet could not root out treacherous disorder and was instead entrapped by it—Madam, observe Shenxi: am I a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi replied: "I have enjoyed the emperor's great favor all my life and was raised to the chancellorship, yet I failed to eradicate the corrupt and have instead been framed. Tell me honestly—do I look like a traitor?"

sentences.zh: 因相與泣下。

translations.literal: Thereupon they wept together.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife wept together.

sentences.zh: 申錫自居內廷，及為宰相，以時風侈靡，居要位者尤納賄賂，遂成風俗，不暇更方遠害，且與貞元時甚相背矣。

translations.literal: From the time Shenxi dwelt in the inner court and became chief minister, because the temper of the age was extravagant and officials in key positions especially accepted bribes, it had become custom; he had no leisure to change ways and keep harm at a distance, and this was greatly at odds with the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: From his service in the inner court through his chancellorship, Shenxi found that extravagance prevailed and officials in high office routinely accepted bribes—a custom so entrenched that he could not easily reform it, and one that contrasted sharply with the standards of the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 申錫至此，約身謹潔，尤以公廉為己任，四方問遺，悉無所受。

translations.literal: Shenxi up to this point restrained himself carefully and cleanly, especially taking public integrity as his charge; gifts sent from all directions, he entirely refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi nonetheless held himself to strict personal discipline and made public integrity his watchword, refusing every gift sent from any quarter.

sentences.zh: 既被罪，為有司驗劾，多獲其四方受領所還問遺之狀，朝野為之嘆息。

translations.literal: Once he was charged with crime, the responsible offices verified and impeached; they recovered many records of gifts sent from all quarters that he had received and returned; court and countryside sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: When officials investigated after his conviction, they uncovered numerous records of gifts offered from every direction—gifts Shenxi had accepted only to send back untouched. The discovery moved officials and commoners alike to sigh in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，卒於開州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the seventh year, he died at Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 833 he died at Kai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「申錫雖不能周慎，自抵憲章，聞其亡歿遐荒，良用悲惻。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Although Shenxi could not be thoroughly cautious and has himself reached the statutes, hearing that he died in a distant wild region, we are deeply moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Although Shenxi failed to exercise sufficient care and brought the law upon himself, learning that he died in a remote frontier post fills Us with deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 宜許其歸葬鄉里，以示寬恩。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to permit his return for burial in his home district, to show broadened favor.
translations.idiomatic: He shall be permitted burial in his home district as a sign of clemency.

sentences.zh: 開成元年九月，詔復申錫正議大夫、尚書左丞、同中書門下平章事、上柱國，賜紫，兼贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Kaicheng, an edict restored Shenxi as Grand Master of Discussion, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Upper Pillar of State, granted purple robes, and also posthumously made him Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In September 836 an edict restored Shenxi's ranks of Grand Master of Discussion, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and Upper Pillar of State, granted him the purple robe, and posthumously appointed him Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 仍以其子慎微為城固縣尉。

translations.literal: His son Shenwei was moreover made Commandant of Chenggu County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenwei was also appointed commandant of Chenggu County.

sentences.zh: 李程李程，字表臣，隴西人。

translations.literal: Li Cheng—Li Cheng, courtesy name Biaochen, a native of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, whose courtesy name was Biaochen, was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父鹔伯。

translations.literal: His father was Subo.
translations.idiomatic: His father's name was Subo.

sentences.zh: 程，貞元十二年進士擢第，又登宏辭科，累辟使府。

translations.literal: Cheng, in the twelfth year of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi and was selected, also passed the Hongci examination, and was repeatedly recruited to commissioners' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: In 796 Li Cheng passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Hongci literary examination; he served on several successive commissioner staffs.

sentences.zh: 二十年，入朝為監察御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he entered court as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 804 he entered the capital as Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 其年秋，召充翰林學士。

translations.literal: That autumn, he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: That same autumn he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，為王叔文所排，罷學士。

translations.literal: When Shunzong acceded, he was sidelined by Wang Shuwen and removed as academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Wang Shuwen forced him out and he lost his Hanlin appointment.

sentences.zh: 三遷為員外郎。

translations.literal: Through three promotions he became Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he reached the rank of Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 元和中，出為劍南西川節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: During Yuanhe, he went out as Campaigning Adjunct Military Commissioner of Western Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he was posted as campaigning adjutant of the Western Chuan military commissioner in Jiannan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年，入為兵部郎中，尋知制誥。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he entered as Director in the Ministry of War; soon he was charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 815 he returned to the capital as Director in the Ministry of War and soon after was charged with drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 韓弘為淮西都統，詔程銜命宣諭。

translations.literal: When Han Hong was Supreme Commander of Huaixi, an edict ordered Cheng to bear the command and proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Hong served as supreme commander of Huaixi, the emperor ordered Li Cheng to carry the imperial message and deliver the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜中書舍人，權知京兆尹事。

translations.literal: The next year, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter and was given provisional charge of Metropolitan Prefect affairs of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Secretariat Drafter and given provisional authority as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 十二年，權知禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was given provisional charge of the Ministry of Rites examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 817 he was given provisional charge of the Ministry of Rites civil-service examination.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 818 he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六月，出為鄂州刺史、鄂嶽觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he went out as Prefect of Ezhou and Observer of E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: That June he was posted as prefect of E Prefecture and observer of the E-Yue circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎，封渭源男，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Vice Minister of Personnel, was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiyuan, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Vice Minister of Personnel, was enfeoffed as Baron of Weiyuan, and granted a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位之五月，以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month after Jingzong's accession, with his existing office he became Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month after Emperor Jingzong's accession, he retained his existing post and was made co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 敬宗沖幼，好治宮室，畋遊無度，欲於宮中營新殿。

translations.literal: Jingzong was young and impulsive, fond of building palaces, hunting without measure, and wished to build a new hall within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was still a boy, fond of palace construction and hunting without restraint, and now wished to erect a new hall within the palace.

sentences.zh: 程諫曰：「自古聖帝明王，以恭儉化天下。

translations.literal: Cheng remonstrated, saying: "Since antiquity sage emperors and enlightened kings have transformed the realm through reverence and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng remonstrated: "Since antiquity, sage emperors and enlightened kings have transformed the realm through reverence and frugality.

sentences.zh: 陛下在諒闇之中，不宜興作，願以瓦木回奉園陵。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is in the period of mourning seclusion; it is not fitting to undertake construction. I pray you redirect the tiles and timber to supply the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still in mourning seclusion—it is not fitting to undertake new construction. I beg that these tiles and timbers be redirected to the imperial tombs instead."

sentences.zh: 上欣然從之。

translations.literal: The emperor gladly followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gladly assented.

sentences.zh: 程又奏請置侍講學士，數陳經義。

translations.literal: Cheng also memorialized requesting the appointment of lecturing academicians, and repeatedly expounded the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng also memorialized for the appointment of lecturing academicians and repeatedly expounded the classics before the throne.

sentences.zh: 程辯給多智算，能移人主之意。

translations.literal: Cheng was eloquent and shrewd in calculation, able to shift the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng was quick-witted and resourceful, and knew how to turn the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 尋加中書侍郎，進封彭原郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Vice Director of the Secretariat and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Pengyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and advanced in rank to Duke of Pengyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，罷相，檢校兵部尚書、同平章事、太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli, he was removed from the chancellorship and made Acting Minister of War, Co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Prefect of Taiyuan, Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital, and Hedong Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 826 he was dismissed from the chancellorship and appointed acting Minister of War, co-signer of the Secretariat and Chancellery, prefect of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 太和四年三月，檢校尚書左僕射、平章事、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Taihe, he was made Acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Minister, Prefect of Hezhong, and Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 830 he was appointed acting Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, chief minister, prefect of Hezhong, and military commissioner of the Hezhong-Jin-Jiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 六年，就加檢校司空。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was additionally made Acting Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 832 he was additionally appointed acting Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 七月，征為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was recalled to the capital as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中謝日奏曰：「臣所忝官上禮，前後儀註不同。

translations.literal: On the day of his central audience of thanks he memorialized, saying: "The ceremonial precedence for the office I undeservedly hold differs in the records before and after.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his formal audience of thanks he memorialized: "The court ceremony prescribed for the office I undeservedly hold has differed in the regulations before and since.

sentences.zh: 在元和、長慶中，僕射數人上日，不受四品已下官拜。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe and Changqing eras, on the investiture days of several Vice Directors, they did not accept bows from officials of fourth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe and Changqing eras, on their investiture days several vice directors refused to receive bows from officials of fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 近日再定儀註，四品已下官悉許受拜，王涯、竇易直已行之於前。

translations.literal: Recently the ritual regulations were revised again: officials of fourth rank and below are all permitted to bow—and Wang Ya and Dou Yizhi have already practiced this before.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations were recently revised again to permit bows from all officials of fourth rank and below, and Wang Ya and Dou Yizhi have already followed this practice.

sentences.zh: 今御史臺云：『已聞奏，太常侍定取十五日上』。

translations.literal: Now the Censorate says: 'We have heard the memorial; the Court of Ceremonies is set to conclude on the fifteenth.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the Censorate reports: 'Your memorial has been received; the Court of Ceremonies will finalize the matter on the fifteenth.'

sentences.zh: 臣進退未知所據。」

translations.literal: In advancing or retreating, your subject does not know what to follow."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know which practice I should follow."

sentences.zh: 時中丞李漢以為受四品已下拜太重。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Han held that accepting bows from officials of fourth rank and below was too weighty an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Han argued that receiving bows from officials of fourth rank and below conferred too great an honor.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「僕射上儀，近已詳定。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The court ceremony for the Vice Director has recently been fully determined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The court ceremony for the vice director has recently been fully determined.

sentences.zh: 所緣拜禮，皆約令文，已經施行，不合更改。

translations.literal: The bowing rites in question all follow the statutes; they have already been implemented and should not be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The bowing rites in question all follow the statutes; they are already in force and must not be altered.

sentences.zh: 宜準太和四年十一月六日敕處分。」

translations.literal: Let it be disposed of according to the edict of the sixth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taihe."
translations.idiomatic: Dispose of the matter according to the edict of the sixth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taihe."

sentences.zh: 程藝學優深，然性放蕩，不修儀檢，滑稽好戲，而居師長之地，物議輕之。

translations.literal: Cheng's artistic learning was deep and excellent, yet his nature was unrestrained; he did not maintain ritual propriety, was given to wit and jest—and yet occupied the position of an elder mentor, so public opinion looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng's learning in the arts was deep and excellent, yet his nature was unrestrained: he neglected ritual decorum, loved wit and jest, and because he held a senior mentor's station, public opinion held him lightly.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，檢校司空、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, he was made Acting Grand Master of Works, Prefect of Bianzhou, and Xuanwu Army Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 833 he was appointed acting Grand Master of Works, prefect of Bian Prefecture, and military commissioner of the Xuanwu Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，復為河中晉絳節度使，就加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he again became Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner and was additionally made Acting Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In 835 he again became military commissioner of the Hezhong-Jin-Jiang circuit and was additionally appointed acting Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 開成元年五月，復入為右僕射，兼判太常卿事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Kaicheng, he again entered [the capital] as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, additionally overseeing the Court of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 836 he returned to the capital as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and was additionally charged with overseeing the Court of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十一月，兼判吏部尚書銓事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he additionally oversaw the Ministry of Personnel selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was additionally charged with overseeing personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，檢校司徒，出為襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, he was made Acting Grand Minister of Education and went out as Prefect of Xiangzhou and Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 837 he was appointed acting Grand Minister of Education and posted as prefect of Xiang Prefecture and military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒，有司謚曰繆。

translations.literal: He died; the responsible office posthumously titled him Miu.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and the responsible offices gave him the posthumous title Miu—"Erroneous."

sentences.zh: 子廓。

translations.literal: His son was Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuo.

sentences.zh: 廓進士登第，以詩名聞於時。

translations.literal: Kuo passed the jinshi examination and was famed in his time as a poet.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo passed the jinshi examination and won renown in his day as a poet.

sentences.zh: 大中末，累官至潁州刺史，再為觀察使。

translations.literal: In the late Dazhong era, through repeated promotions he reached Prefect of Yingzhou and twice served as observer.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Dazhong era he rose through successive posts to prefect of Ying Prefecture and served twice as a circuit observer.

sentences.zh: 廓子晝，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: Kuo's son Zhou also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo's son Zhou also passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：宗儒、易直，以寬柔養望，坐致公臺；

translations.literal: [Comment] The Historian comments: Zongru and Yizhi, by mildness and forbearance nurtured reputation, attained the chief ministries without effort;
translations.idiomatic: [Comment] The Historian comments: Zongru and Yizhi cultivated reputation through mildness and forbearance and attained the chief ministries without striving;

sentences.zh: 與時沈浮，壽考終吉，可謂能奉身矣。

translations.literal: Drifting with the times, living long and dying well—it can be said they knew how to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They drifted with the times, lived long, and died in peace—one may say they knew how to preserve themselves.

sentences.zh: 逢吉起徒步而至鼎司，欺蔽幼君，依憑內豎，蛇虺其腹，毒害正人，而不與李訓同誅，天道福淫明矣。

translations.literal: Fengji rose from commoner to reach the tripartite chancellorship, deceived the young ruler, relied on inner eunuchs, harbored vipers in his belly, poisoned upright men—yet was not executed alongside Li Xun; that Heaven favors the wicked is plain.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji rose from commoner to the tripartite chancellorship, deceived the young emperor, relied on palace eunuchs, harbored vipers in his breast, and poisoned upright men—yet escaped execution alongside Li Xun. That Heaven favors the wicked could not be plainer.

sentences.zh: 申錫小器大謀，貶死為幸。

translations.literal: Shenxi—small vessel, grand design; death in demotion was his fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxi was a small man with grand designs; to die in exile was his good fortune.

sentences.zh: 程不持士範，歿獲醜名。

translations.literal: Cheng did not maintain the scholar's standard; in death he obtained an ugly posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng failed to uphold the scholar's standard and in death earned an ugly posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 君子操修，豈宜容易！

translations.literal: The gentleman's self-cultivation—how can it be taken lightly!
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman's self-cultivation—how lightly it must never be taken!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：趙、竇優柔，坐享公侯。

translations.literal: In praise: Zhao and Dou, gentle and yielding, sat and enjoyed marquisates and dukedoms.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Zhao and Dou, gentle and yielding, sat at ease and enjoyed the ranks of marquis and duke.

sentences.zh: 蝮蛇野葛，逢吉之流。

translations.literal: Vipers and wild aconite—the ilk of Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Vipers and wild poison—the kind to which Fengji belonged.

sentences.zh: 豈無令人？

translations.literal: Was there not a worthy man?
translations.idiomatic: Was there not a worthy man among them?

sentences.zh: 主輔謨猷。

translations.literal: Chief minister in counsel and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister of counsel and strategy.

sentences.zh: 程、錫弼諧，於道難周。

translations.literal: Cheng and Xi as supporting ministers—in the Way, hard to be complete.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Xi as chief ministers—in the Way, they could not be whole.
